conclusions: YOLO26-N pixels-to-CPU-boxes: ours is faster on the tested inputs. Native photograph about 11.8-12.0 ms vs ruNNtime 15.1 ms; 1280x720 crop about 13.0-13.4 ms vs 18.5-18.6 ms, across two independent runs.

YOLO GPU compute totals are closer: ruNNtime about 9-12% slower, depending on run/input. Extra wall time also occurs outside compute (CPU preprocessing/encoding/decoding, transfers/readback and browser scheduling); do not assign the whole difference to convolution kernels.

ruNNtime has useful native conv wins: first YOLO 3x3 RGB layer about 1.8x and the 16-to-8 output-channel 3x3 layer about 2.1x. Our tested YOLO attention matmuls and several larger convolutions are faster.

Other native wins include tiny-spatial split-K pointwise, matrix-vector products and a 576-channel 5x5 depthwise case. These particular benchmark shapes occur in neither current model program. They are general operator opportunities, not a demonstrated model gain.

DepthART is not the same architecture: our export is MNV4-S, while the published ruNNtime small checkpoint is MobileMamba-S (source metadata relative_s_448). Our half weights are about 4.1 MB vs the 12.6 MB ruNNtime checkpoint. Timing both tasks is valid, but attributing their roughly 2x difference to the runtimes is not.
No production kernel, graph, shader registry or model artifact was changed. Native operators ran inside ruNNtime, with named exports added to a generated copy solely to access its unpublished core.

method.primary: Two independent Chrome runs, one shared GPU adapter/device per task, shader-f16 and subgroups enabled. 12 warmups, 61 alternating-order samples per input/engine, batch1. CPU RGBA bytes to CPU depth map or class/score/xyxy boxes, including processing/upload/inference/readback/decoding. Image decoding, model downloading/compilation, camera capture and rendering are excluded.
method.inputs: Same photograph at native square model size, the photograph at 1280x720 with center crop, and a deterministic gradient at native size. This is a latency/correctness probe on three inputs, not a dataset accuracy or COCO mAP study.
method.imageProcessing: ruNNtime uses its public crop preprocessor. Our helper uses the existing GPU preprocessing shaders; non-native images use the example-style canvas crop. Interpolation and FP16 casting/fusion ordering can differ. YOLO confidence .35 and maximum 64 detections on both.
method.gpu: Separate 15-sample timestamp phase; primary wall samples contain no timestamps. Sum compute-pass spans, including model and input-conversion/preprocess kernels, excluding CPU and buffer/texture copies. Diagnostic wall/residual fields pair wall and GPU times in that phase. Do not subtract GPU medians from a different phase to reconstruct a latency breakdown: GPU clocks can change.
method.nativeOperators: 25 native-layout cases: 15 FP16 convolutions plus 5 matrix geometries in each precision. We expose native entry points from the pinned compiled package without changing implementations. Native HWC4 input/weight packing, uploads and graph recording occur outside timing. Each library caches its own kernel selection/command list. 8 warmups, 41 alternating GPU samples, 16 replays per sample; no fused activation/residual in raw conv cases.
method.numerics: YOLO public outputs match local FP32 references: all expected detections match class and IoU >=.8 with confidence difference <=.05 and no extra detections on these inputs. Raw operators validate all finite outputs and relative L2 <=3% against rounded F32 references; measured errors/maxima are retained. Native FP16 matmul uses wider accumulation, improving accuracy relative to our FP16 path on these inputs. DepthART models have different scales and opposite sign conventions; cross-model correlation is descriptive, not a correctness requirement.
method.kernelMembership: modelReferenceCounts counts matching operator input/weight geometry and stride (conv) or trailing matrix dimensions (mm/bmm). A zero means that exact benchmark geometry is absent from that model.
method.limits: One M1 Pro and Chrome build. Timing ratios describe this hardware/browser; cross-hardware portability and gains require separate measurements. Cold-start load timings are diagnostic and not directly comparable because setup paths differ.

runs.method: Published ruNNtime 0.1.0 vs our unchanged graphs; paired pixels-to-CPU-results and separate GPU compute times. See per-case model equivalence and numerical validation.
runs.warning: DepthART backbones differ (ours MNV4-S, ruNNtime MobileMamba-S); DepthART is a workload comparison, not an isolated runtime benchmark. YOLO26-N uses the same task/variant and input size.

nativeKernels.method: Published package implementation plus named exports only. Native conv uses HWC4/mat4 weight packing; ours uses NCHW. Packing, upload, graph capture and correctness readback excluded. No activation/residual fusion in these raw cases. Both libraries select their own kernels. 8 warmups, 41 alternating GPU timestamp samples, 16 replays per sample, one recorded invocation per submit, summed GPU compute duration divided by 16. Validation requires relative L2 error <=3% for these FP16 accumulation workloads and records max absolute error. F16 numerical differences compared with F32 on identical rounded dyadic inputs. These are native-layout cached-input microbenchmarks; use whole-model results for application performance.
